negative_results_and_repairs: First segmented prototype was slower than full-copy maintenance because a global per-pulse safety hash and N-query segment verification accidentally destroyed locality; those hot-path O(N) checks were removed in favor of immutable segment identities plus slower audits.

The first content-id design hashed per-path dependency sets while persistence retained only the segment-wide dependency union, making exact deep reconstruction impossible. V16 changes content identity to the exact persisted physical representation and adds a slow corruption audit.

Bootstrap remains slower than the simple full-generation baseline in the measured synthetic fixture; V16 is therefore not a universal replacement and should be used only when measured update locality amortizes the extra bookkeeping.
limitations: Synthetic clustered topology is deliberately locality-friendly; real Frank/Clay dependency fan-out is not measured here.
Path compilation is deterministic Python proxy work; downstream GWT/model/tool outcome quality is not measured.
The comparator is full generation copying, not every conventional database design.
An exact indexed SQLite/B-tree path remains the proper latency floor when a resolved key is already known.
Remote Hostinger and final Andreas Ubuntu target execution remain required before promotion.
